draft.title: Optimisation
card: Optimisation finds the largest or smallest value of a quantity. First write that quantity as a function of one variable. Use any given condition to remove the other variables.
Differentiate and solve f'(x) = 0 to find the stationary points. Test each one to see if it is a maximum or minimum, using the second derivative or the sign of f'(x) on each side.
Check the endpoints of the allowed domain, because the greatest or least value can occur there. Also check that the answer makes sense, for example that a length is positive.

Example: two numbers add to 10. Find the largest product. If one is x, the other is 10 − x, so P = x(10 − x) = 10x − x². Then P' = 10 − 2x = 0 gives x = 5. P'' = −2 is negative, so it is a maximum. The largest product is 5 × 5 = 25.
draft.remember: Write one variable, solve f'(x) = 0, test the type, then check endpoints and sense.

a.q: Two numbers add to 12. Their product P = x(12 − x). What is the largest value of P?
a.why: P = 12x − x², so P' = 12 − 2x = 0 gives x = 6. P'' = −2 is negative, so this is a maximum, and P = 6 × 6 = 36. The value 6 is where the maximum occurs, not the maximum itself.
a.clue: Find x first, then put it back into P.

b.q: Ava has 40 m of fencing for a rectangular pen with width x metres and length y metres. Which area A is largest, using A = x(20 − x) with 0 ≤ x ≤ 20?
b.why: A = 20x − x², so A' = 20 − 2x = 0 gives x = 10. A'' = −2 is negative, so it is a maximum, and A = 10 × 10 = 100. The endpoints x = 0 and x = 20 both give area 0, so they are smaller. The value 10 is the width, not the area.
b.clue: Find x, then work out the area, and compare with the endpoints.

problems.detail: The stem 'Which area A is largest' reads as asking which listed option is the largest number, which would be 400 m². It should ask 'What is the largest possible area A?'

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct (36 and 100 m²). Question b's wording 'Which area A is largest' is ambiguous and could point students to 400 m², so it should be reworded to 'What is the largest possible area?'
